request.input:
You repair a Boolean network model of the DNA damage response (a published model, Gupta et al. 2023).
A claim read from the literature was turned into a rule change by a fixed template, and an exact solver rejected the
change: the edited network contradicts behaviours the model must keep (the verification cases). Propose another rule
for the node that still expresses the claim but passes those cases.

Rules are written with node names and the operators ! (not), & (and), | (or) and parentheses. A node is 1 when active.
DNA_damage is the only input. These are the nodes you may use: AKT, AMPK_MAPK, ATM_pH2AX, ATR, BAX, BCL2, CHK1, CHK2, Caspase, Cdc25, Cdc2_CycB, DNA_PK, DNA_damage, E2F1, Mdm2, Myc, PTEN, PUMA, RB, Sirt1, TUG1, ULK1_Beclin1, WWP1, Wee1, Wip1, hTERT, mTORC1, mTORC2, miR221, p21, p53, p53_A, p53_INP1, p53_K

CLAIM: Caspase inhibits AKT   (1 paper(s))
EVIDENCE:
- PMC3759859 (p53-induced apoptotic processes, review statement): "In turn, p53-induced apoptotic processes can commit AKT to cleavage by executioner caspases, thereby creating a feedback loop to protect cells from the adverse effects of AKT [40]."

NODE TO CHANGE: AKT
CURRENT RULE:   AKT, mTORC2 & (!PTEN | DNA_damage)
TEMPLATE RULE (rejected): AKT, (mTORC2 & (!PTEN | DNA_damage)) & !Caspase

WHY IT WAS REJECTED (counterexamples from the solver; "setting" fixes nodes to 0 or 1, a phenotype is read from the
fixed points; the witness is a fixed point of the edited network):
- V02 (Section 3.2, damage: the four stable fates); setting {'DNA_damage': 1}: missing; expected phenotypes ['apoptosis', 'arrest', 'autophagy', 'senescence'] (exact), found ['arrest', 'autophagy', 'senescence']; witness fixed point {'DNA_damage': 1, 'p53': 1, 'p53_A': 1, 'p53_K': 0, 'p21': 1, 'Wip1': 1, 'Cdc2_CycB': 0, 'PTEN': 1, 'AKT': 0, 'mTORC1': 0, 'mTORC2': 0, 'ULK1_Beclin1': 0, 'BAX': 0, 'Caspase': 0}
- V03 (Figure 3, TUG1 E1); setting {'DNA_damage': 1, 'TUG1': 1}: missing; expected phenotypes ['apoptosis', 'arrest', 'autophagy', 'senescence'] (exact), found ['arrest', 'autophagy', 'senescence']; witness fixed point {'DNA_damage': 1, 'p53': 1, 'p53_A': 1, 'p53_K': 0, 'p21': 1, 'Wip1': 1, 'Cdc2_CycB': 0, 'PTEN': 1, 'AKT': 0, 'mTORC1': 0, 'mTORC2': 0, 'ULK1_Beclin1': 0, 'BAX': 0, 'Caspase': 0}
- V07 (Figure 3, TUG1 E1 + miR-221 KO); setting {'DNA_damage': 1, 'TUG1': 1, 'miR221': 0}: missing; expected phenotypes ['apoptosis', 'arrest', 'autophagy', 'senescence'] (exact), found ['arrest', 'autophagy', 'senescence']; witness fixed point {'DNA_damage': 1, 'p53': 1, 'p53_A': 1, 'p53_K': 0, 'p21': 1, 'Wip1': 1, 'Cdc2_CycB': 0, 'PTEN': 1, 'AKT': 0, 'mTORC1': 0, 'mTORC2': 0, 'ULK1_Beclin1': 0, 'BAX': 0, 'Caspase': 0}
- V09 (Table 1 row 10, PTEN E1 + WWP1 KO (a prediction of the paper)); setting {'DNA_damage': 1, 'PTEN': 1, 'WWP1': 0}: missing; expected phenotypes ['apoptosis', 'arrest', 'autophagy', 'senescence'] (exact), found ['arrest', 'autophagy', 'senescence']; witness fixed point {'DNA_damage': 1, 'p53': 1, 'p53_A': 0, 'p53_K': 1, 'p21': 0, 'Wip1': 0, 'Cdc2_CycB': 0, 'PTEN': 1, 'AKT': 0, 'mTORC1': 0, 'mTORC2': 0, 'ULK1_Beclin1': 1, 'BAX': 1, 'Caspase': 1}

Requirements, all checked by the solver afterwards:
- Caspase must be able to switch AKT off and never on: it acts on AKT only in the direction 'inhibits'.
- Keep every influence the current rule has: every node in the current rule must still affect the new rule in the same way.
- Use only the nodes listed above. Do not use AKT in its own rule.
- You may restrict WHEN the claimed effect applies by combining it with other nodes, if the evidence context (cell
  type, condition) or the counterexample suggests a condition. Say which condition you chose and why. Do not invent a
  mechanism the evidence does not support.
- If no rule can both express the claim and pass the cases, set give_up to true and explain.

Answer as JSON: {"rule": "<expression only, no node name and no comma>", "explanation": "...", "give_up": false}.

text: {"explanation": "Kept base activation mTORC2 & (!PTEN | DNA_damage) and made Caspase inhibition conditional on absence of DNA_damage: AKT = base & (!Caspase | DNA_damage). When DNA_damage=1 the rule reduces exactly to the current rule, preserving the required DNA-damage fates (V02,V03,V07,V09 all have DNA_damage=1). When DNA_damage=0, Caspase can switch AKT off. Condition chosen from counterexamples (all failures have DNA_damage=1 where DNA_damage-driven AKT maintenance must be kept); evidence is a generic review statement about p53-induced cleavage, not specific to acute DNA-damage decision, so limiting scope to non-DNA-damage context retains claim direction without inventing new mechanism.", "give_up": false, "rule": "mTORC2 & (!PTEN | DNA_damage) & (!Caspase | DNA_damage)"}
